bugs.summary: WebRTC ICE consent-refresh times out mid-session against OpenAI Realtime API media server, dropping the connection on second user speech turn (Firefox 150)

comments.author: omer.fisher@gmail.com
comments.creator: omer.fisher@gmail.com
comments.raw_text:
User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:150.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/150.0

Steps to reproduce:

1. In Firefox 150 (Windows 11), open a page that establishes a WebRTC peer
   connection to OpenAI's Realtime API:
     POST https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls?model=gpt-realtime-1.5
     Content-Type: application/sdp
   The offer contains one audio sendrecv m-section (Opus) and one
   DataChannel ("oai-events"). ICE gathering uses defaults (no TURN).

2. After applying the answer SDP, wait for iceConnectionState === "connected"
   and dataChannel.onopen, then send a session.update event configuring
   instructions / VAD / transcription / output voice, followed by
   response.create.

3. Allow the AI to deliver its response (~30–90s of inbound TTS audio over RTP).

4. After receiving response.done and output_audio_buffer.stopped, begin
   speaking into the microphone to start a second user turn (input_audio_
   buffer.speech_started fires).


Actual results:

Within 5–10 seconds of input_audio_buffer.speech_started on the second user
turn, the connection drops:

  [rt-event] response.done                       ← AI finishes turn 1
  [rt-event] output_audio_buffer.stopped
  [rt-event] input_audio_buffer.speech_started   ← user starts turn 2
  [rt-ice-state] disconnected                    ← drop, 5–10s later
  [rt-conn-state] disconnected
  [rt-dc-close] readyState: closed

about:webrtc shows several successful ICE consent-refresh exchanges
followed by `STUN-CLIENT(consent): Timed out`. No application-level error
event is signalled by the server before the drop — only routine
rate_limits.updated events, then the closing connection-state transitions.

100% reproduction across 10+ sessions, two networks (residential WiFi +
mobile hotspot), normal mode and private mode, Firefox desktop and Firefox
on Android.

Testing matrix already exhausted on the client side (none changed the
outcome): semantic_vad → server_vad; full prompt → slim 500-char prompt;
language hint dropped; explicit STUN+TURN added (UDP-direct candidate pair
confirmed via getStats); session.update mid-session disabled; client noise
gate bypassed; output GainNode bypassed; getUserMedia with all browser
audio processing (echoCancellation, noiseSuppression, autoGainControl)
disabled; whisper-1 vs gpt-4o-mini-transcribe; SDP munged with usedtx=0
and cn=0; continuous near-silent comfort tone injected upstream during AI
playback; addTransceiver with explicit sendrecv direction instead of
addTrack; bundlePolicy: max-bundle + rtcpMuxPolicy: require (this one
made the drop instant — likely incompatible with the server's answer).


Expected results:

The session should remain connected through the second user turn and
subsequent turns, as it does in Chrome (latest) and Edge (latest) with
identical client code, identical OpenAI account, identical model
(gpt-realtime-1.5), and identical session.update payload — both browsers
run 5+ minute sessions through many turns without drops.

The OpenAI Realtime Playground also works on Firefox 150, but a DevTools /
about:webrtc inspection confirms the Playground uses WebSocket transport,
not WebRTC. This isolates the bug to the WebRTC media path specifically.

Suspected regression introduced in Firefox 150. MFSA 2026-30 lists six
WebRTC-related fixes shipped in 150:

  - Bug 2021769 (CVE-2026-6747) — UAF in WebRTC
  - Bug 2027499 (CVE-2026-6752) — boundary conditions in WebRTC
  - Bug 2027501 (CVE-2026-6753) — boundary conditions in WebRTC
  - Bug 2021768 (CVE-2026-6775) — boundary conditions in WebRTC
  - Bug 2021770 (CVE-2026-6776) — boundary conditions in WebRTC: Networking
  - Bug 2029461 (CVE-2026-7321) — sandbox escape in WebRTC: Networking

The "incorrect boundary conditions" cluster is a plausible source of new
packet validation that may now reject edge-case STUN consent-refresh or
RTCP packets the OpenAI media server emits, but I have not yet confirmed
which fix is responsible. A bisect against Firefox ESR 128.x / 140.x and
Nightly is the next step I can run if it would help.

comments.author: docfaraday@gmail.com
comments.creator: docfaraday@gmail.com
comments.raw_text:
None of those bugs have anything to do with ICE consent I'm afraid, and I'd be surprised if this were a recent regression, because we only recently fixed a bug that allowed us to connect at all (https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2034159). If you can determine otherwise with mozregression, please let us know.

I'm going to guess this is a site issue of some sort, but it is impossible to tell what that issue is without more information.

* Maybe OpenAI is not responding to consent checks on a connection it intends to keep using; that would be a bug on their end. If Chrome and/or Safari are letting consent timeouts slide, that's a bug on their end.
* Maybe OpenAI does *not* intend to keep the connection alive, and is either not performing an ICE restart later on when the browser is Firefox (their bug), or is performing that ICE restart in a way we do not support (maybe our bug), or that the spec does not support (their bug).

I might be able to glean some more information if you attached a copy of about:webrtc to this bug.

comments.author: omer.fisher@gmail.com
comments.creator: omer.fisher@gmail.com
comments.raw_text:
Minimal reproduction page deployed: https://firefox-webrtc-repro.vercel.app/

Single static HTML file, ~150 lines, no dependencies. Reproduction steps are on the page itself — paste an OpenAI API key with realtime access, click Connect, speak briefly after the AI greeting. Drop happens within 5-10 seconds of input_audio_buffer.speech_started.

One refinement to the original report: in this run the drop fired on the third user turn rather than the second (turns 1 and 2 completed cleanly, then 9s into turn 3's speech_started the ICE state went to disconnected). So the failure isn't strictly tied to "the second turn" — it's more "within the first few user turns once the mic starts transmitting again post-AI-output." 100% repro across runs in the same session, just the exact turn varies.

Source visible in browser view-source for inspection.

Sample log from one reproduction run:


[14:42:32.029] [ice-state] connected
[14:42:34.058] [dc] open
... (turns 1 and 2 completed normally) ...
[14:43:01.333] [event] input_audio_buffer.speech_started   ← turn 3 mic on
[14:43:10.334] [ice-state] disconnected                    ← 9 seconds later
[14:43:10.334] [conn-state] disconnected

comments.author: docfaraday@gmail.com
comments.creator: docfaraday@gmail.com
comments.raw_text:
Nightly, 149, and ESR all lose their connection; this does not appear to be a regression. Chrome and Safari appear to work. There are a few differences between our consent checks and theirs:

* Ours are paced every 5 seconds, in accordance with RFC 7675. Theirs are paced at about 3 seconds, which violates RFC 7675.
* Theirs contain a (proprietary and not-standardized) GOOG-NETWORK-INFO STUN attribute.
* Theirs contain a USE-CANDIDATE STUN attribute, which is nonsensical in a consent check.
* Ours have PRIORITY before ICE-CONTROLLING, theirs is the other way around; this is fine and nothing should care.

I am not sure which (if any) of these is making the difference here, but if any of them are the cause, that's a bug on OpenAI's end.

comments.creator: docfaraday@gmail.com
comments.raw_text:
A local build that puts USE-CANDIDATE in consent checks (provided we're in the controlling role, which we are in this case) seems to work.

OpenAI needs to ignore USE-CANDIDATE in consent checks. That is only meaningful in ICE checks.

comments.author: omer.fisher@gmail.com
comments.creator: omer.fisher@gmail.com
comments.raw_text:
Thank you, Byron — building a local patch that adds USE-CANDIDATE to
consent checks and confirming it works is the definitive evidence I
couldn't have produced from the application side.

Three takeaways from your analysis:

- This is not a Firefox 150 regression. Bug 2034159 made connection
  possible at all; before that, the consent-check issue was simply
  invisible.

- Firefox is correct per RFC 7675 / 8445 — USE-CANDIDATE has no defined
  semantics in consent checks. OpenAI's media server appears to either
  require it or treat its absence as invalidating the check. Chrome and
  Safari coincidentally satisfy this requirement by including
  USE-CANDIDATE non-compliantly.

- There is no client-side workaround.

I've filed this with OpenAI on their developer forum (the post hasn't
been allowed external links yet due to a new-account restriction. One additional developer (TimoP_imc) has already
chimed in on that thread independently confirming the same symptom, with
a similar "worked recently, broken now" framing — so it may be that a
recent OpenAI server change exposed (or introduced) the USE-CANDIDATE
requirement. The webcompat:site-bug tag should also help Mozilla's
webcompat team reach OpenAI through their own channel.

Thanks again.

comments.author: omer.fisher@gmail.com
comments.creator: omer.fisher@gmail.com
comments.raw_text:
Update 2026-05-30: still reproducing in Firefox 151.0 against the production OpenAI Realtime endpoint via WebRTC. Same drop signature — ice-state: disconnected ~30-60s in, right after the 2nd user speech turn.

Interesting wrinkle: same Firefox 151 build + same OpenAI account gives different results between two payload sizes. A simplified standalone repro (~500-char prompt, raw getUserMedia) passed 3 consecutive sessions cleanly. Our production integration (~35K-char system prompt, semantic_vad, AudioContext + GainNode + noise gate) drops reliably. Possibly relevant to your USE-CANDIDATE diagnostic — different candidate-pair selection under different SDP / audio-transport conditions? Speculating.

Multiple users on the OpenAI Developer Forum thread (ingsplazas May 21 on Firefox 151.0, plus TimoP, bearly_p, vb, Prashant) also report Firefox 151 still reproduces. Happy to provide additional repro data, about:webrtc dumps, or run mozregression if useful.

Anything new on the OpenAI contact side since comment 15?
